The statement balances clear acknowledgment of pandemic-driven downside risks with a forcefully accommodative policy stance. This aligns with the Financial Stability Report’s findings that, while vulnerabilities remained elevated and the outlook uncertain, Federal Reserve actions—near-zero policy rates, large-scale Treasury and agency MBS purchases, repo operations, and emergency facilities—helped ensure market functioning, restore short-term funding markets, and support the flow of credit to households and businesses. The average-inflation-targeting framework (allowing inflation moderately above 2% for a time) aims to keep expectations anchored near 2%, consistent with the FSR’s emphasis on policy support mitigating financial stress. Net tone: cautious on the outlook but materially supportive on policy, warranting a slightly negative yet improved sentiment versus a risk-only reading.
